newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO official says it tries to curb rights abuses.
newsitem.headline: PLO official says it tries to curb rights abuses.

text.p: An aide to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Monday said there were some human rights violations in the West Bank and Gaza but added the Palestinian Authority was trying to curb them.
Marwan Kanafani, commenting on an Amnesty International report issued on Monday, insisted the abuses were not official policy in self-rule areas under the Authority's control.
Amnesty charged that human rights violations, including mass arrests of political opponents and torture, had increased over the past two years and produced an atmosphere of fear among Palestinians.

"We know there are some violations of human rights in our country. We are against that and we have to find solutions to stop that," Kanafani, who is also a member of the Palestinian Legislative Council, told reporters in Gaza.
"We are sorry that such things happen in our country...The only positive thing I could say now is that this is not the policy of the government," he said.
The London-based human rights group said "victims of brutal torture" and other abuses were afraid to speak out or give their names, in a "growing climate of fear".
Amnesty said Palestinian journalists who reported abuses were arrested, their newspapers closed down and prominent human rights activists faced harassment.
Kanafani said some members of the Palestinian security forces had committed human rights violations.

"The fact is that there are some people who take the law into their own hands. Sometimes there are some generals who are inolved in such things," he said. "We have never heard about such an incident without taking the corrective measures."
Amnesty said its delegations, including medical personnel, had visited the Palestinian self-rule areas several times and documented abuse by various Palestinian security services.

It said mass detentions of suspected opponents of the peace process had been carried out following pressure by Israel and the United States to clamp down on those responsible for violent attacks on Israeli citizens.

The Palestinian Authority should use internationally recognised standards to bring to justice those who had committed violent acts and there was no justification for the use of torture and other serious human rights abuses, said Amnesty.
It said at least nine people had died in the custody of the Palestinian security services in circumstances where torture appeared to have caused or contributed to their deaths.

The legal system had been "marginalised and ignored" as political detainees were held with no reference to any law. Few of those arrested made any attempt to hire a lawyer as "they know it will make no difference", Amnesty said.
